title: AITA For Getting My Wife Deported?
question: AITA For Getting My Wife Deported?
body:
Background: My (ex) wife is Korean and I basically knocked her up briefly after we met. I married her after our son was born and we moved to the US about 2 years ago. 

I knew from the start wasn’t quite right with her, but she didn’t tell me until much later she has borderline and bipolar. That said, she could be sweet and was relatively smart. 

After our son was born, she started drinking heavily. She would be violent towards me (arrested a few times, but I always dropped the charges... I know.) and would attempt to commit suicide about once a month (mostly pills). 

I filed for divorce and left her a few months ago. She cleaned up her act, got some new doctors, and sobered up. She begged me to take her back and give her another chance because she had “changed”, so I caved. 

Since then, things had been ok. Not awful, but not normal either. She definitely wasn’t what I needed in a wife or our son needed in a mother. I grew impatient with her lack of progress, but to be fair she was making some progress. She was just unable to help with all the responsibilities involved in having a child, was a drag financially, didn’t make me happy, and was simply a bad role model for our son with her fits, outbursts and screaming. 

So one day after a particularly bad set of fights and her relapsing into violence and suicide attempts, I told my lawyer that I wanted to continue with the divorce and no longer wanted to sponsor her visa. 

So obviously I stuck it out with her longer than I should have and have go ven her plenty of chances, so I don’t feel bad for leaving her. But I feel like an asshole because unlike most people who get a divorce, now she won’t physically be around to see her son grow up since she was deported and can likely never come back (due to some visa issues since before we met). Does that make me an asshole?
